title: Harbour Lights Night Market 2027: campaign run from workshop to published site
domain: campaign design: whiteboard, presentation, marketing assets, web
deliverable: One campaign, four linked deliverables: a workshop board with votes and a CSV of decisions; a 14-slide 16:9 launch deck as PDF; a marketing set of 4 formats by 6 stallholders (24 PNG files, a logo SVG and a poster PDF); and a responsive 2-page landing site published as static files to a local target folder.
status_rule: callable = a RUN_COMMANDS id, CLI verb or public Viewer or LayoutEditor method that was read and can be called now. engine_only = public crate logic exists and was read, but no command or host reaches it. missing = searched and not found; evidence names each search, and the build of this file re-ran it with git grep at the revision and required zero hits. Every file:line was resolved at that revision by the same build; every clause line was resolved in the spec file. Nothing was built or run: callable is present and read, not proven working. agent_call.reach separates corpus or CLI from a Rust-only method. runs_only_on_stand_in marks a callable step whose real target does not exist yet.

workflow_basis.method: Step order paraphrased from public vendor help articles, found by search on 2026-11-07; search summaries were read, not every full article. No vendor text or asset was copied. Names in this file are the spec's. The help pages may be dated.
unverified: Figma Make prompt-to-app flow (step 87): the search returned nothing on it, so the step is UNVERIFIED against that product.
Publishing here is deliberately a static export to the operator's own target (STU-WEB-006), which differs from the vendor's hosted publishing.
parity_points_that_exceed_the_spec: The vendor's presenter notes and notes-plus-audience presenting (steps 41, 53) have no clause in module 14.
The vendor's bulk create also sets asset size per row; this project covers sizes in steps 70 and 76.

comparison.board: Read node records and tally as JSON; compare the CSV byte for byte; compare PNG by pixel values against a stored expected render.
comparison.deck: Compare page count and text extracted from the PDF, then render each page to an image and compare at a set tolerance. A screen fit does not prove a PDF fit.
comparison.assets: 24 files with exact names and pixel sizes; decode each and compare the field text regions; compare SVG by parse, not bytes.
comparison.site: Compare published bytes by sha256 against the export; re-parse with hsk_studio_web::parse and assert an empty loss report; preview_tree at 360, 768 and 1280 asserts which elements render and which rules are active; pixel comparison waits for web.capture_view.

gaps.why_it_ranks_here: The cheapest route from nothing to a published deliverable. The engine is tested but stranded, static publishing to a folder needs no server or network, and a model can already judge output by source, preview_tree and hashes before any pixels exist.

gaps.what: No way to start or structure a design job: no blank document command, no artboard creation, and export covers only the whole document. Twenty-four named outputs cannot exist.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Every scene's first step depends on it, and it unlocks the marketing set, whose drawing tools already work. It shares a root with the vector, print and web scenarios, so one fix pays several times.

gaps.what: The deck stops short of a PDF and of being a deck: fixed A4 pages, no image placing, no PDF export from a host, and no slide role, skip, timing, grid or slide transition binding. Layout editing itself is reachable.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: 13 of 31 steps already call, and the engines for size, placement, PDF and transitions exist. Host wiring plus one role record yields a real exported deck.

gaps.what: Board mode does not exist: no node kind beyond Layer, Artboard and PageSpread, no record, no viewer, no router, no command, no export. All twelve node kinds and connectors are absent. The whole workshop is blocked.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: It blocks the most steps, and one whole deliverable; a mechanical count would put it first. It sits fourth because nothing can be reused toward an end result, and STU-WB-101 itself calls this the lowest-priority parity domain. Sticky, section and connector alone would be a usable first slice.

gaps.what: No web rendering. The web crates evaluate no layout and paint nothing, so web.capture_view, the live, split and inspect views and the breakpoint ruler all have nothing beneath them. Needs a decision: own a layout and paint engine for the subset, or another route. The spec requires it and forbids nothing here, but names no engine.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Few steps, but it is the visual proof for the whole site and for the responsive claim. A person cannot judge the page in Studio without it. It ranks below the source-level route only because that route ships a site first and proves more of the workflow.

gaps.what: Most callable steps are Rust methods. Only 6 of 29 callable steps are a corpus or CLI command; slides, layout and vector drawing have no command_id. The drive loop will not reach them.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: It decides whether a model can run this project as a script. Lower than the deliverable gaps because a Rust runner can bridge it for now.

gaps.what: No batch or proposal path at the host: StudioCommandBatch and the command builder do not reach the harness, so a generated diagram, a prompt-made page, and a bulk run cannot be one reviewable undo.
